headline: Cochise County land due diligence: flood, soil, and elevation from free public data
metaDescription: What the free government data shows for Cochise County, Arizona — FEMA flood-zone read, dominant SSURGO soils, and elevation band for land investors, with named sources.
intro: Before you buy vacant land in Cochise County, three free federal datasets tell you most of what kills a resale: the FEMA flood zone, the dominant soil order (which drives septic feasibility), and the elevation band. AcreOS runs all three on every parcel — here is the county-level read, with sources.

figures.note: Cochise sits high in southeastern Arizona — even valley-floor parcels are well above flood stage, but the range means slope and access vary sharply across the county.

figures.note: Cochise's high-desert basin-and-range soils are dominated by arid-zone orders with frequent caliche — perc-test and septic feasibility is the buyer's real diligence cost.

figures.note: Flood risk concentrates in FEMA-mapped washes and the San Pedro / Sulphur Springs valley floors; pull the parcel's NFHL zone before you buy.

dataSnapshot.disclaimer: Figures are a Cochise County reference read from public federal datasets and do not replace a parcel-level lookup. Coverage and currency vary by county GIS; always pull the parcel's own FEMA NFHL zone, SSURGO map unit, and 3DEP elevation before relying on these.

faq.q: Is land in Cochise County in a flood zone?
faq.a: It depends on the parcel. Flood risk concentrates in FEMA-mapped washes and the San Pedro / Sulphur Springs valley floors; pull the parcel's NFHL zone before you buy. The only reliable answer is the parcel's own FEMA NFHL zone, which the free AcreOS parcel check pulls in seconds.

faq.q: What kind of soil does Cochise County have?
faq.a: Cochise's high-desert basin-and-range soils are dominated by arid-zone orders with frequent caliche — perc-test and septic feasibility is the buyer's real diligence cost. For a specific parcel, the SSURGO map unit gives you the exact soil series and its septic-suitability rating.

faq.q: Do I need to pay for data to do diligence in Cochise County?
faq.a: No. The flood, soil, and elevation reads above come from free federal datasets (FEMA, USDA NRCS, USGS). AcreOS runs them on every parcel at no cost; you only reach for paid data providers once your deal volume earns it.
